rooms.title: The Entrance
rooms.label: Warm-Up
rooms.content:
Two periods, one garden 🌱 A plant cannot walk, cannot talk, and cannot hide — so it has a plan, and the plan is called a life cycle. Today you learn the words for every step of it, then you build the cycle with your own hands.

  • Eight words — the parts of a plant and the things that happen to them
  • The order of the cycle: seed → sprout → flower → fruit → seed
  • Why a flower bothers to be bright and full of nectar
  • The project: cut, fold, assemble, and say it in order

rooms.title: The School Garden
rooms.label: Scene
rooms.content:
Mai: Look — the bean seed I planted last week has a tiny green shoot coming out 🌱
Nam: That is a sprout, right? The first thing that comes out of the seed.
Mai: Yes. And the whole thing — the seed waking up and starting to grow — is called germination.
Nam: So it needs water and warmth? Because the one I left dry is still just a hard seed.
Mai: Water, warmth and air. Take away one of them and nothing happens.
Nam: And then it grows a flower. Then the bees come. Then there is a fruit with new seeds inside it.
🤔 Reality check: the seed is not dead and the fruit is not the end. A seed is a plant waiting, and the fruit is a seed carrier. The cycle only looks like a line — it is a circle that starts again.

rooms.title: The Group Chat
rooms.label: Text Scene
rooms.content:
Nam: ok so why r flowers so bright. just to look nice?? 🌸
Mai: no lol. the colour and the smell are advertising. theyre saying COME HERE to the bees
Nam: and the nectar?
Mai: thats the payment. bee gets nectar, flower gets pollination — the bee carries pollen from one flower to the next
Nam: so the bee is basically a delivery driver that doesnt know it 😂
Mai: exactly that. no delivery, no seeds. no seeds, no new plants. thats why pollination matters
Text Clues: in a life-cycle question, look for which stage the sentence is about — germination and sprout belong to the beginning, pollination and nectar belong to the flower, and seed closes the circle.

rooms.title: The Words
rooms.label: Learn
rooms.content:
1. seed: the hard little case that holds a baby plant and its food — the beginning of the cycle.
2. germination: the seed waking up and starting to grow. It needs water, warmth and air.
3. sprout: the first tiny green shoot that pushes out of the seed. The sign that germination worked.
4. stem: the part that holds the plant up and carries water from the roots to the leaves.
5. flower: the bright part of the plant — its job is to make seeds, and colour is how it calls the insects.
6. pollen: the fine yellow dust a flower makes. Move it to another flower and seeds can begin.
7. pollination: pollen travelling from one flower to another — by a bee, a butterfly, the wind, or a hand.
8. fruit: the part that grows around the seeds and protects them until they are ready to travel.

rooms.title: The Life Cycle
rooms.label: Reading
rooms.content:
1. Seed. A hard case with a baby plant and a small store of food inside. It can wait a long time — months, sometimes years.

2. Germination. Water, warmth and air arrive. The seed cracks and a root goes down, then a shoot goes up.

3. Sprout and plant. Green leaves open and start making food from sunlight. The stem grows taller.

4. Flower. The plant grows petals, colour and nectar. This is the plant's way of calling an insect.

5. Pollination. A bee lands for the nectar and walks through the pollen. It flies to the next flower, and the pollen goes with it.

6. Fruit and seed. The flower changes into a fruit, and inside the fruit there are new seeds. The fruit falls, or an animal carries it away — and the cycle starts again.
🤔 Reality check: every stage exists to make the next seed. The flower is not decoration and the fruit is not a prize — they are the two parts of the plant's transport system.

rooms.title: The Project
rooms.label: Project
rooms.content:
Build the life cycle (SP_Grade 5).

1. Cut the six stage cards out along the lines.
2. Fold each card on the middle line so the picture faces out.
3. Assemble the cards into a circle — seed, germination, sprout, flower, pollination, fruit and seed — and glue the last one back to the first.
4. Write one short sentence on the back of each card: "This is ______. It happens after ______."
5. Say your cycle out loud to your partner, from the seed all the way round.
Pro Tip: if you can say the cycle out loud without looking at the cards, you have finished the project — the paper is only there to get the order into your head.

rooms.title: Game 1 — Plant Scramble
rooms.label: Game 1
rooms.content: How to win: the letters are shuffled. Click them in the right order to rebuild the word, then read what it means. Eight words — and the last one closes the circle.

rooms.title: Game 2 — Part & Job
rooms.label: Game 2
rooms.content: How to win: click the part of the plant on the left, then its job on the right. Wrong pairs shake and let go — guess boldly.

rooms.title: Game 3 — Order the Cycle
rooms.label: Game 3
rooms.content: One word per station: BEGINNING · MIDDLE · END — put each piece of the cycle in the part it belongs to.

rooms.title: The Test
rooms.label: Test
rooms.content:
Scenario: You plant a bean seed, water it, and three days later a tiny root and shoot appear. What is this stage called?
Scenario: A bee lands on a flower for nectar, and when it flies away there is yellow dust stuck to its legs. What is that dust called?
Scenario: Which stage of the life cycle comes both before the young plant and out of the fruit at the end?

rooms.title: The Key
rooms.label: Mastery
rooms.content:
🌸 You can now walk the whole life cycle out loud
  • Six stations, one circle: seed → germination → sprout → flower → pollination → fruit & seed.
  • A seed needs three things: water, warmth and air. Take away one and germination never starts.
  • The flower is advertising: colour and nectar are how it calls an insect — and pollination is the payment.
  • Pollen travels, seeds are made: no pollination means no seeds, and no seeds means no new plants.
  • The fruit is a carrier, not an ending: it protects the seeds until they can travel — and then the cycle begins again.
Level Up: find one flowering plant at home or on the way home tonight. Say the cycle out loud for that plant, in order, in front of somebody: seed, germination, sprout, flower, pollination, fruit and seed. Then tell them which stage it is in right now.
Write it down: pick one stage and explain what the plant is doing during it — two full sentences, using the stage's own word.
